children: BTCUSD slid from ~$80–85k to mid-$70k late October, hitting intraday lows near $76.3k after a $6.3B Binance hack; withdrawals paused, exchange to cover losses; >$1.6B liquidations; ~5–7% monthly drop
BTCUSD spot CFD: Binance froze about $3B in on-chain funds and paused deposits/withdrawals amid probes of unusual transfers from Binance-labeled wallets; losses to be covered by SAFU and reserves.
BTCUSD saw ongoing institutional buys as U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs held over $104 billion in net assets, signaling large capital inflows into Bitcoin-focused funds.
VanEck launched WBMO, an active multi‑asset ETF with ~2% targeted Bitcoin allocation (1%–5%), gaining BTCUSD spot exposure via a spot Bitcoin ETP rather than direct holdings.
Morgan Stanley bought about 1,302 BTC via its MSBT spot Bitcoin trust for over $100M, lifting the fund's total holdings to roughly 10,850 BTC.
Analysts say recent Binance troubles don't yet threaten BTCUSD solvency, but large outflows or customer losses could spark wider deleveraging if withdrawals turn disorderly.
BTCUSD traded near the 50-week SMA around $76,000 after a Binance-linked sell-off; buyers stepped in and price stabilized, with the 50-week SMA acting as key technical support.
BTCUSD spot saw $292M net outflow over 30 days to Oct 26, 2026—the first 30‑day net outflow since July; outflows were smaller than earlier waves and inflows resumed later in the week.
Stacks founder Muneeb Ali warned quantum computing poses long-term risks to Bitcoin. He urged a shift to quantum-resistant keys by ~2028–2030, noting possible impact on BTCUSD demand.
Analyst Benjamin Cowen sees two near-term BTCUSD paths: a sharp single-day drop or a bounce then later fall. BTCUSD is on cycle day 389, resembling the 2014–2015 bottoming pattern.
